name: Madrid

sights.name: Cathedral
sights.content: It is the centrepiece of Toledo. It sits on top of the hill and is deceptively large. When you enter you will be confronted by sparkling gold reliefs, huge oil paintings and portraits of all of the Toledo Cardinals going back at least 500 y

sights.name: Iglesia de los Jesuitas
sights.content: It offers ''great views'' of Toledo and the surrounding region from its twin spires. It is set in the highest location in the city. (Oct-Mar 10:00-17:45, Apr-Sep 10:00-18:45)

sights.name: Mosque of Cristo de la Luz
sights.content: It was built 1000 years ago as a small mosque, but 200 years later was converted to a church. The building itself is a mix of the two styles, with a primarily Mudejar architecture, and early Christian paintings on the walls. (mid Oct-Feb 10

sights.name: Iglesia del Salvador
sights.content: It was like the Mezquita Cristo de la Luz converted from a mosque into a church, though in this case the architecture of the building is more varied, combining Mudejar, Visigoth, and Roman-style architecture. (mid Oct-Feb 10:00-17:45, Mar-m

sights.name: The Burial of the Count of Orgaz
sights.content: One of El Greco's most famous and recognized works, it's housed in '''Iglesia de Santo Tomé'''. (Mid Oct-Feb 10:00-17:45, Mar-Mid Oct 10:00-18:45)

sights.name: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca
sights.content: It's one of the three synagogues that remain in Spain from before the expulsion of the Jews in the 16th century, two of which are in Toledo (the third is in Córdoba). (mid Oct-Feb 10:00-17:45, Mar-mid Oct 10:00-18:45)

sights.name: Monastery of San Juan de los Reyes
sights.content: It's a beautiful 16th century church in the Jewish quarter that was built by Ferdinand and Isabella to house their tombs. Upon the conquest of Granada, they decided to be buried there instead, but it is still easily worth the visit. (mid Oc
sights.en: Monasterio de San Juan de los Reyes

sights.name: Synagogue of El Tránsito
sights.content: The second of Toledo's remaining pre-16th century synagogues, it hosts the Sefardi Museum.

sights.name: The Alcazar
sights.content: A large square building on the outskirts of the old city. It looks across the river at Franco's old military barracks. The origin of the building dates back to the presence of a Roman camp in the 3rd century. The Muslims built there a keep

sights.name: El Greco Museum
sights.content: The El Greco Museum offers an intimate look into the life and work of Doménikos Theotokópoulos, showcasing a collection of his paintings alongside period furnishings in a reconstructed 16th-century Toledo setting.

sights.name: Museum of the Army
sights.content: The Museum of the Army is housed in the imposing Alcázar of Toledo, a historic fortress overlooking the city. It presents the history of the Spanish Army from its early origins to the modern era, with exhibits ranging from medieval weapons

foodDrink.name: Patata y Olé
foodDrink.content: Variety of baked potatoes, cooked differently than elsewhere. They have vegan options and they are super friendly. The attention and the atmosphere are unbeatable, the site is very nice.

foodDrink.name: Bar Ludeña
foodDrink.content: Family tavern where details and flavors are taken care of without nonsense. A good place to eat typical Toledo food. Good carcamusas with their spicy touch.

foodDrink.name: La Cuesta de Toledo
foodDrink.content: Typical Castilian food and very familiar and pleasant treatment. Mostly locals inside. Quaint and unassuming.

foodDrink.name: Bar Skala
foodDrink.content: Local food, simple and delicious, wonderful waiters and gluten-free options. Very nice place and good atmosphere.

foodDrink.name: La Mona Bar
foodDrink.content: A small and cozy place, with a good menu of tapas. Very good are the typical carcamusas from Toledo and the casserole. Awesome burgers and good service.

foodDrink.name: La Casa de Damasco
foodDrink.content: Excellent little place down a back alley. Extensive menu, incredible flavors, very kind treatment.

foodDrink.name: El Rinconcito
foodDrink.content: Super homemade tapas. Very goodh cocretah and paellah. Nice atmosphere and treatment.

foodDrink.name: Restaurante Trébedes Toledo
foodDrink.content: Everything is super tasty. The waiters are super attentive and friendly. Extensive menu.

foodDrink.name: Malpica Retro
foodDrink.content: A charming place. Great treatment, great food and a good atmosphere. Curiously appetizing.

foodDrink.name: Restaurante Pizzería Il Padrino
foodDrink.content: Delicious pizzas, spectacular dough, super fast and good service.

foodDrink.name: La Ramona - Toledo
foodDrink.content: It is a cafeteria with a large terrace. Everything is simple. A quality tapas bar.

foodDrink.name: Meson de la Orza
foodDrink.content: Great food, great service, not so cheap, but it is worthy. Dishes include; lomo de orza, pork tenderloin; migas, a traditional Spanish breadcrumb dish served with lamb sweetbreads; roast suckling lamb and pig; partridge on arroz meloso; and

foodDrink.name: Madre Tierra
foodDrink.content: All organic food with vegan and vegetarian offerings, smoothies, and an organic wine list.

guideSights.name: Torres de Colón
guideSights.note: Eye-catching twin towers, constructed 1967–74. With 116 metres and height and 23 floors, they are among the highest buildings in Madrid.

guideSights.name: Plaza de Olavide
guideSights.note: Circular place and nice green space (thanks to the motorised traffic being directed through a tunnel), surrounded by an ensemble of colourful 19th-century residential buildings.

guideSights.name: Nuevos Ministerios

guideSights.name: Hospital de Maudes
guideSights.note: Former hospital complex, built in 1916 in an eclecticist style (similar to Palacio de Cibeles, that was designed by the same architects). It includes a church, Santa María del Silencio. The hospital was intended to serve the poorer classes,

guideSights.name: Constitutional Tribunal
guideSights.note: Modern circular building from the early 1980s, designed by architects Bonet and Valdés.

guideSights.name: Plaza de Castilla
guideSights.note: On the north side of the city and bisected by Paseo de la Castellana, this plaza is in the center of Madrid's skyscraper district. A tall obelisk sits in the center of the plaza while the '''Gate of Europe''' (''Puerta de Europa'') towers,

guideSights.name: Cuatro Torres
guideSights.note: Four sleek skyscrapers, constructed between 2004 and 2009. Standing 224 to 249 metres tall, they are the highest in Spain. From south to north, they are named Torre Cepsa, Torre PwC, Torre de Cristal, and Torre Espacio. In the latter, the e

guideSights.name: Basílica La Milagrosa
guideSights.note: Church from the 1900s in Neo-Mudéjar and Gothic revival style, dedicated to Our Lady of Miracles.
guideSights.en: Basilica of St. Vincent de Paul

guideSights.name: Casa Gallardo
guideSights.note: Imposing and highly ornamental Art nouveau (or ''modernismo'') building at the western corner of Plaza de España, designed by Federico Arias Rey and completed in 1914.

guideSights.name: Arco de la Victoria
guideSights.note: Francoist triumph arch erected 1950–56 to commemorate the Nationalist victory in the Battle of Ciudad Universitaria of the Civil War.

guideSights.name: Real Ermita de San Antonio de la Florida
guideSights.note: This small church is famous for its murals, painted by Goya. It's also the mausoleum of the painter.
guideSights.en: Royal Chapel of St. Anthony of La Florida

guideSights.name: Parque Madrid Río

guideSights.name: Faunia
guideSights.note: Zoological park. Different sections of the park include animals from different locations (Africa, Antarctica etc..)

guideSights.name: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales

guideSights.name: Spanish National Research Council Headquarters
